To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
for 2 ° C global warming about 21 % of today's land climates will become novel, while about 20 % of today's climates will disappear.
the climate analogs of future projections are novel and disappearing at the same time.
the future seasonal climates at a large fraction of locations are novel and cannot be found in the present.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the emergence of novel and disappearing climates under global warming.
the emergence of novel climate states in a warmer world.
climate analogs and their usefulness for communicating climate change impacts.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
for many places in the world, the future climate is unlike anything that has been observed so far.
the future seasonal climates at most places are not like any current climate, and that this is especially the case in the tropical regions.
for many places the seasonal cycle of future climate will be unlike currently observed anywhere on Earth.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
for a 4°C warming the world would be very different from today.
the concept of spatial analogs, as a tool for visualizing climate change, should be used with care.
climate change is not only about warming but also about the disappearance of many present-day climates and the emergence of novel ones, which is a challenge for the future of life on Earth.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the concept of spatial climate change analogs should be used with caution, and that the full seasonality of climate should be accounted for when using analogs for visualizing and discussing climate change.
climate change may be a driver of novel climates, which is a concept not widely used in the literature.
the climate analog concept should be interpreted with caution, as it can be misleading when applied to seasonal climate projections, especially for the tropics and the polar regions.
